style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: A matte clay 3D assembly in a server room, placed on a brushed-steel service floor: a modular storage bay with a sprung checkpoint latch held open, a segmented timer cam, and a coiled write-head cable resting against it, all coloured graphite, bone white, and safety yellow. A single key light rakes from the left across the matte surfaces, throwing long contact shadows to the right and leaving generous negative space on the right. Three-quarter off-centre composition, weathered concrete base, no text, no logos.

rationale: The article is a structural and mathematical economics story about checkpoint intervals and lost compute time, with no literal scene to photograph. A small matte 3D assembly of recognisable engineered parts can state the checkpoint gap tradeoff with mechanical clarity, and the Nano Banana Pro build idiom supports precise part arrangement and lighting.
subject: a modular storage bay with a sprung checkpoint latch, segmented timer cam, and coiled write-head cable
core_thesis: Spot discount's real cost is the checkpoint gap — the interval between state saves that determines how much work a preempted job throws away; at Meta's measured failure rate with a one-minute write, that gap is about 19 minutes.
core_conflict: a cheap spot rate versus an unpredictable reclaim timer, where write cost and failure gap squeeze effective compute time.
composition: asymmetric off-centre framing with three-quarter perspective and generous negative space on the right

review.depicts: A blocky modular cuboid unit made of grey, cream and yellow segments sits open-fronted on a pale ledge, with a hinged latch mechanism inside the opening, a segmented fan-like disc leaning at its front-right corner, and a coiled yellow-and-grey cable with a connector plug resting beside it, against a background of dark perforated server cabinets.
review.reason: The frame shows the ordered mechanism — storage bay, latch, segmented timer cam, coiled write-head cable — in a server-room setting, so it reads as the article's checkpoint/write mechanism rather than a different industry, though the cost-per-19-minutes claim itself is only implied.
